I've been running the Texas Method for a few weeks and my squat/deadlift keep progressing at the rate they should, but my OHP has stalled and my bench has not only stalled, but it's gone down! I'm eating a ~300 cal surplus and sleeping plenty, so I don't think external factors are the issue. Would it be a good idea to try switching to SS for the upper body lifts and lower them 15% to build them back up?

If it matters, my stats are:

5' 11, 163 lbs

Squat 5x235

Deadlift 5x300

OHP 5x110

Bench 5x175

googles texas method

.....

Ah, Mark Rippetoe. Naturally, he has you squatting first thing every single workout. shakes head

The thing about squats is, they put a ridiculous amount of stress on your whole body. So, by the time you get to your presses, you are probably too exhausted to use your full strength, and thus make lackluster gains.

My suggestion, and this is the best I can do without completely modifying the program, would be to switch up the order and press first, at least every other workout. Your squat gains will still be there, in fact, they're not likely to change at all, considering how much less stressful pressing is.

But your press gains will definitely go up.

Well Justin Lascek himself said that the upper body part is neglected in his E-Book Texas Method and that if someone is looking to get a bigger bench/OHP they should take from somewhere else, I'd recommend Bill Starr 5x5 (Especially the Madcow 5x5 variant is great for Bench). Make sure you add lots of back work and now you have a good excuse to do curls as well, generally don't skip on the accessory for bench.
